questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Drawing & Design in a technical project?
options: To communicate ideas for making or improving products
To decorate paper with unrelated patterns
To replace all workshop safety rules
To hide dimensions from the maker
questions.correctAnswer: To communicate ideas for making or improving products
questions.explanation: Drawing and design help learners plan, communicate, test, and improve practical solutions before production.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of drawing and design in communicating technical ideas.

questions.prompt: Which item is a basic instrument for drawing circles and arcs accurately?
options: Compass
Hacksaw
Spanner
Paint roller
questions.correctAnswer: Compass
questions.explanation: A compass holds a fixed radius from a centre point, making circles and arcs accurate.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify drawing instruments and their uses.

questions.prompt: Which drawing instrument is mainly used to measure and construct angles?
options: Protractor
Claw hammer
File
Bench vice
questions.correctAnswer: Protractor
questions.explanation: A protractor has angle graduations used to measure or set out angles in degrees.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify instruments used for accurate geometrical construction.

questions.prompt: Which information is normally included in a technical drawing title block?
options: Drawing title, scale, date, and name of the drawer
Only the cost of lunch
Only the colour of the paper
Only the number of classroom windows
questions.correctAnswer: Drawing title, scale, date, and name of the drawer
questions.explanation: A title block identifies the drawing and gives key information needed to interpret it.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify information recorded in a drawing title block.

questions.prompt: Which line type is commonly used to show visible edges of an object?
options: Continuous thick line
Dashed hidden line
Chain centre line
Freehand break line
questions.correctAnswer: Continuous thick line
questions.explanation: Visible outlines and edges are usually drawn with continuous thick lines so the object shape is clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify standard line types used in technical drawings.

questions.prompt: Which line type is commonly used to show a hidden edge in a technical drawing?
options: Dashed thin line
Continuous thick border
Freehand shading line
Dimension extension line only
questions.correctAnswer: Dashed thin line
questions.explanation: Hidden features are represented by dashed thin lines to show edges that are not directly visible.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise line conventions for hidden features.

questions.prompt: What does a scale of 1:1 mean on a drawing?
options: The drawing is full size
The drawing is twice the actual size
The drawing is half the actual size
The drawing has no measurements
questions.correctAnswer: The drawing is full size
questions.explanation: A 1:1 scale means one unit on the drawing represents one equal unit on the actual object.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret common drawing scales.

questions.prompt: What is dimensioning in technical drawing?
options: Showing sizes and positions on a drawing
Colouring the whole sheet
Cutting material with a saw
Writing a story about a product
questions.correctAnswer: Showing sizes and positions on a drawing
questions.explanation: Dimensions tell the maker the lengths, widths, diameters, angles, and positions needed for production.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of dimensioning in a technical drawing.

questions.prompt: Which view in orthographic projection usually shows the length and height of an object?
options: Front view
Plan view
Right side view only
Auxiliary note
questions.correctAnswer: Front view
questions.explanation: A front view commonly presents the main face of an object, showing its length and height.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify principal views used in orthographic projection.

questions.prompt: Which orthographic view is commonly called the plan?
options: Top view
Front view
End view
Section note
questions.correctAnswer: Top view
questions.explanation: The plan is the view seen from above, so it is also called the top view.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the plan view in orthographic drawings.

questions.prompt: Which pictorial drawing shows three faces of an object with equal-looking axes commonly set at 30 degrees from the horizontal?
options: Isometric drawing
Flow chart
Bar graph
Ledger account
questions.correctAnswer: Isometric drawing
questions.explanation: Isometric drawing represents three dimensions on axes that are equally inclined, helping show a 3D form on paper.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify isometric drawing as a pictorial representation method.

questions.prompt: In oblique drawing, which face is usually drawn in its true shape?
options: Front face
Back shadow
Title block
Hidden edge only
questions.correctAnswer: Front face
questions.explanation: Oblique drawing begins with the front face in true shape, then depth is projected backward.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic features of oblique projection.

questions.prompt: What does CAD stand for in drawing and design?
options: Computer-aided design
Class attendance diary
Cutting and drilling
Colour arrangement display
questions.correctAnswer: Computer-aided design
questions.explanation: CAD uses computer software to create, modify, store, and print design drawings.
questions.learningOutcome: Define CAD in the context of drawing and design.

questions.prompt: Which safety item protects the eyes during workshop model-making after a design drawing is prepared?
options: Safety goggles
Drawing paper
Notebook cover
Set square
questions.correctAnswer: Safety goggles
questions.explanation: Safety goggles protect the eyes from dust, chips, and small particles during practical production tasks.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify personal protective equipment used during design practical work.

questions.prompt: Which stage of the design process comes before selecting the best solution?
options: Generating possible ideas
Painting the finished product only
Throwing away all sketches
Ignoring the user need
questions.correctAnswer: Generating possible ideas
questions.explanation: Designers first explore several possible ideas before judging and selecting the most suitable solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify stages in the design process.

questions.prompt: Which term means a quick drawing made to communicate an idea before detailed work?
options: Sketch
Invoice
Receipt
Welding bead
questions.correctAnswer: Sketch
questions.explanation: A sketch quickly records a design idea and helps discussion before a detailed drawing is prepared.
questions.learningOutcome: Define sketching as a tool for communicating design ideas.

questions.prompt: Why should construction lines be drawn lightly?
options: They guide the drawing and can be erased without spoiling the final lines
They must be darker than all visible outlines
They replace all dimensions on the drawing
They are used only to colour the title block
questions.correctAnswer: They guide the drawing and can be erased without spoiling the final lines
questions.explanation: Light construction lines help locate features accurately and can be removed or left faint after final outlines are completed.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain good practice when preparing neat technical drawings.

questions.prompt: Why is a border important on a technical drawing sheet?
options: It frames and protects the working area of the drawing
It changes the scale automatically
It replaces the need for a title block
It shows the price of all materials
questions.correctAnswer: It frames and protects the working area of the drawing
questions.explanation: A border defines the drawing space and gives the sheet a clear, professional layout.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of borders and layout on drawing sheets.

questions.prompt: Why are drawing instruments stored dry and clean after use?
options: To maintain accuracy, prevent damage, and keep drawings neat
To make the instruments heavier
To turn all lines into hidden lines
To reduce the size of the drawing paper
questions.correctAnswer: To maintain accuracy, prevent damage, and keep drawings neat
questions.explanation: Clean, dry instruments last longer and help produce accurate, smudge-free drawings.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how to care for drawing instruments and materials.

questions.prompt: What is the advantage of using standard line conventions in a technical drawing?
options: Different readers can interpret the drawing in the same way
The drawing can be made without measurements
The paper becomes waterproof
The product cost is removed
questions.correctAnswer: Different readers can interpret the drawing in the same way
questions.explanation: Standard line conventions give shared meaning to outlines, hidden details, centre lines, and dimensions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why standard drawing conventions support technical communication.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains a centre line?
options: It shows the centre of a circle, hole, or symmetrical feature
It shows only the outside visible edge
It marks a place for writing a price
It is used to shade every surface
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the centre of a circle, hole, or symmetrical feature
questions.explanation: Centre lines help locate axes of symmetry and the centres of circular features.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret the function of centre lines in technical drawings.

questions.prompt: Why should dimensions be written clearly and not repeated unnecessarily?
options: Clear non-repeated dimensions reduce confusion during making
Repeated dimensions always improve accuracy
Missing units make the drawing easier to use
Dimensions are only for decoration
questions.correctAnswer: Clear non-repeated dimensions reduce confusion during making
questions.explanation: Good dimensioning gives enough information for production while avoiding conflicting or cluttered measurements.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe qualities of clear dimensioning in technical drawings.

questions.prompt: In scale drawing, what does a scale of 1:5 mean?
options: One unit on the drawing represents five units on the object
Five units on the drawing represent one unit on the object
The drawing is full size
The drawing has five title blocks
questions.correctAnswer: One unit on the drawing represents five units on the object
questions.explanation: A 1:5 scale is a reduction scale, so the real object is five times the drawing measurement.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret reduction scales used in technical drawing.

questions.prompt: Why are large objects often drawn using a reduced scale?
options: So they fit on available drawing paper while keeping proportions
So all measurements become random
So no title block is needed
So the object becomes smaller in real life
questions.correctAnswer: So they fit on available drawing paper while keeping proportions
questions.explanation: A reduced scale lets a large product be represented clearly on a manageable sheet.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain when to use reduced scale in technical drawing.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between first-angle and third-angle projection symbols?
options: They show which orthographic projection system is used
They show the selling price of the product
They show the type of pencil used
They replace the plan and front views
questions.correctAnswer: They show which orthographic projection system is used
questions.explanation: Projection symbols tell the reader how the views are arranged and interpreted.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of projection symbols in orthographic drawings.

questions.prompt: Why are orthographic drawings useful to a craftsperson?
options: They show exact views and dimensions needed to make a part
They show only a colourful impression without sizes
They hide important details from the maker
They remove the need for measuring tools
questions.correctAnswer: They show exact views and dimensions needed to make a part
questions.explanation: Orthographic drawings present true shapes and sizes in separate views for accurate production.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the use of orthographic projection in technical communication.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a plan view of a rectangular box?
options: It shows the box as seen from above
It shows the box as seen from inside only
It shows only the hidden bottom edges
It shows the title block enlarged
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the box as seen from above
questions.explanation: The plan view is produced by looking down on the object from above.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the direction used to obtain a plan view.

questions.prompt: Why is isometric drawing often used when presenting a design idea to a client or class?
options: It gives a clear 3D impression of the product
It hides the product depth
It lists all costs without showing shape
It shows only one flat face
questions.correctAnswer: It gives a clear 3D impression of the product
questions.explanation: Isometric drawings help viewers visualise length, width, and height at the same time.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of pictorial drawing in design presentation.

questions.prompt: What is the main advantage of cabinet oblique over cavalier oblique for long objects?
options: Cabinet oblique reduces depth distortion by drawing depth at half size
Cabinet oblique removes the front face
Cabinet oblique uses no receding lines
Cabinet oblique makes all dimensions invisible
questions.correctAnswer: Cabinet oblique reduces depth distortion by drawing depth at half size
questions.explanation: Shortening the depth in cabinet oblique makes the pictorial view look less stretched.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the difference between cabinet and cavalier oblique drawings.

questions.prompt: What does a sectional view show in a technical drawing?
options: Interior details after an imaginary cut through the object
Only the colour of the object
Only the package label
The object without any hidden or visible lines
questions.correctAnswer: Interior details after an imaginary cut through the object
questions.explanation: A sectional view reveals internal features that may be difficult to understand from outside views alone.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of sectional views in technical drawings.

questions.prompt: What does hatching usually indicate in a sectional drawing?
options: Material cut by the cutting plane
The title block area
A hidden screw thread only
A place for writing the scale
questions.correctAnswer: Material cut by the cutting plane
questions.explanation: Hatching marks the solid material exposed by the imaginary cut in a section.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret hatching conventions in sectional drawings.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an assembly drawing?
options: To show how separate parts fit together
To show only one raw material price
To replace every part drawing with a poem
To hide fastening positions
questions.correctAnswer: To show how separate parts fit together
questions.explanation: Assembly drawings communicate the relationship, order, and fit of parts in a product.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of assembly drawings in product design.

questions.prompt: What is a development in sheet-material design?
options: A flat pattern that can be folded to form a 3D object
A random drawing with no dimensions
A finished product painted only on one face
A list of absent learners
questions.correctAnswer: A flat pattern that can be folded to form a 3D object
questions.explanation: Development shows the true shapes of surfaces so sheet material can be cut and folded accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe development as a flat pattern for three-dimensional forms.

questions.prompt: Why is a seam or glue tab added to a carton development?
options: To provide an overlap for joining the folded surfaces
To make the drawing scale disappear
To show the front view only
To replace all fold lines
questions.correctAnswer: To provide an overlap for joining the folded surfaces
questions.explanation: A tab gives extra material for glue, tape, or another joining method when forming the package.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the function of joining tabs in package developments.

questions.prompt: Why are layers useful in CAD software?
options: They organise different drawing elements such as outlines, dimensions, and construction lines
They make the computer heavier
They prevent all files from being saved
They turn every line into a circle
questions.correctAnswer: They organise different drawing elements such as outlines, dimensions, and construction lines
questions.explanation: Layers help control visibility, editing, and plotting of different parts of a digital drawing.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the use of layers in CAD drawings.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner save CAD work with a clear file name?
options: It makes the drawing easier to identify, retrieve, and share
It deletes all old work automatically
It changes the drawing scale without warning
It prevents the need for backup copies
questions.correctAnswer: It makes the drawing easier to identify, retrieve, and share
questions.explanation: Clear file naming supports organisation, collaboration, and future revision of design work.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain good file management practices for digital drawings.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a design brief?
options: To state the problem, users, constraints, and expected solution
To list unrelated jokes for the project
To hide the user need from the designer
To replace all evaluation after making
questions.correctAnswer: To state the problem, users, constraints, and expected solution
questions.explanation: A design brief guides the designer by defining what problem needs to be solved and under what conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of a design brief in product development.

questions.prompt: Why should a designer research users before sketching final ideas?
options: To understand real needs, preferences, and constraints
To avoid asking any useful questions
To copy a product without thinking
To make the final drawing less accurate
questions.correctAnswer: To understand real needs, preferences, and constraints
questions.explanation: User research helps the designer create a solution that fits the people and context it is meant for.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how research informs design decisions.

questions.prompt: Why are several sketches often made before choosing one design?
options: They allow comparison and improvement of different possible solutions
They waste materials during production
They prevent feedback from classmates
They make dimensions unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: They allow comparison and improvement of different possible solutions
questions.explanation: Multiple ideas help designers explore alternatives before selecting and developing the strongest one.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of generating alternative design ideas.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a prototype?
options: To test a design idea before full production
To replace all drawings permanently
To hide problems from users
To avoid improving the product
questions.correctAnswer: To test a design idea before full production
questions.explanation: A prototype helps designers check form, fit, use, and weaknesses before making the final product.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of prototyping in design work.

questions.prompt: Why should designers consider locally available materials?
options: They can reduce cost, improve repairability, and support practical production
They always remove the need for measurements
They make every design identical
They prevent sustainable choices
questions.correctAnswer: They can reduce cost, improve repairability, and support practical production
questions.explanation: Local materials may be easier to source, repair, and use responsibly in school or community projects.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors that influence material choice in design.

questions.prompt: What does ergonomics mainly consider in product design?
options: How well a product fits and supports the human user
How many hidden lines are in a drawing
How to ignore safety during use
How to make every item the same colour
questions.correctAnswer: How well a product fits and supports the human user
questions.explanation: Ergonomics focuses on comfort, safety, reach, posture, and ease of use for people.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ergonomic considerations in product design.

questions.prompt: A learner draws a 300 mm shelf at a scale of 1:5. What length should be shown on the drawing?
options: 60 mm
150 mm
300 mm
questions.correctAnswer: 60 mm
questions.explanation: At 1:5 scale, the drawing length is the actual length divided by 5, so 300 mm becomes 60 mm.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply scale calculations to technical drawings.

questions.prompt: A line on a drawing is 80 mm long at a scale of 1:4. What is the actual length?
options: 320 mm
20 mm
84 mm
40 mm
questions.correctAnswer: 320 mm
questions.explanation: At 1:4 scale, the real length is four times the drawing length, so 80 mm times 4 equals 320 mm.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate actual size from a reduced-scale drawing.

questions.prompt: A small machine part is 15 mm wide but is drawn 45 mm wide. Which scale is being used?
questions.explanation: The drawing is three times the actual width, so the enlargement scale is 3:1.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine enlargement scale from drawing and actual dimensions.

questions.prompt: A designer needs to locate a 10 mm hole at the centre of a square plate. Which drawing feature should be added?
options: Centre lines crossing at the hole position
Random shading across the plate
A price label beside the plate
A freehand border only
questions.correctAnswer: Centre lines crossing at the hole position
questions.explanation: Intersecting centre lines clearly locate the centre of a circular hole or symmetrical feature.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply centre-line conventions to locate circular features.

questions.prompt: A bracket drawing shows a hole diameter but not the distance from the edge to the hole centre. What should be added?
options: A locating dimension from a reference edge to the centre line
Extra colour over the hole
A second title block on the same sheet
A random dashed line away from the part
questions.correctAnswer: A locating dimension from a reference edge to the centre line
questions.explanation: Hole position must be dimensioned from a clear reference so it can be drilled in the right place.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply dimensioning conventions to locate features accurately.

questions.prompt: Which dimensioning method is best when several features are measured from one datum edge?
options: Parallel dimensioning
Random dimensioning
Colour dimensioning
Shaded dimensioning
questions.correctAnswer: Parallel dimensioning
questions.explanation: Parallel dimensioning uses one reference edge or datum, reducing accumulated errors in feature positions.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply datum-based dimensioning to technical drawings.

questions.prompt: A learner must construct a perpendicular bisector of a line segment. Which tool pair is most suitable?
options: Compass and ruler
Hammer and nails
Paint brush and roller
Spanner and pliers
questions.correctAnswer: Compass and ruler
questions.explanation: A compass marks equal arcs from both ends of the line, and a ruler joins the arc intersections.
questions.learningOutcome: Select instruments for constructing perpendicular bisectors.

questions.prompt: To divide a line into six equal parts, which method is most appropriate?
options: Draw an inclined auxiliary line, mark six equal spaces, and project back to the original line
Guess six spaces by eye only
Fold the drawing paper randomly
Use a saw to cut the paper
questions.correctAnswer: Draw an inclined auxiliary line, mark six equal spaces, and project back to the original line
questions.explanation: The auxiliary-line method gives equal divisions accurately without trial and error.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply a construction method for dividing a line into equal parts.

questions.prompt: A regular hexagon is to be constructed inside a given circle. Which length is commonly stepped around the circumference?
options: The radius of the circle
Twice the diameter
Half the circumference by eye
The title-block height
questions.correctAnswer: The radius of the circle
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon inscribed in a circle has each side equal to the radius of the circle.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply circle geometry to construct regular polygons.

questions.prompt: A signboard corner requires a smooth radius joining two straight edges. Which construction is needed?
options: Tangent arc construction
Random zigzag construction
Hidden-line removal
Lettering enlargement only
questions.correctAnswer: Tangent arc construction
questions.explanation: A tangent arc joins straight lines smoothly without a sharp corner.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply tangency when designing rounded corners and transitions.

questions.prompt: A front view shows a rectangle 80 mm by 50 mm, and the top view shows depth 40 mm. What main dimensions define the block?
options: 80 mm length, 40 mm depth, and 50 mm height
80 mm height, 50 mm depth, and 40 mm title
40 mm length, 50 mm radius, and 80 mm angle
50 mm scale, 40 mm border, and 80 mm line type
questions.correctAnswer: 80 mm length, 40 mm depth, and 50 mm height
questions.explanation: The front view gives length and height, while the top view supplies depth.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret dimensions from front and plan views.

questions.prompt: A plan view shows a circular hole as a circle, but the front view passes through the hole sideways. How should the hole appear in the front view?
options: As hidden lines if the hole cannot be seen directly
As a solid black patch
As a price tag
As no feature at all
questions.correctAnswer: As hidden lines if the hole cannot be seen directly
questions.explanation: A through hole that is not visible in a view is represented using hidden lines.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply hidden-line conventions when drawing unseen features.

questions.prompt: When projecting from a front view to a plan view, why are projection lines kept thin and light?
options: They help align features without competing with final outlines
They are the final visible edges
They replace all measured dimensions
They are used to shade the finished drawing
questions.correctAnswer: They help align features without competing with final outlines
questions.explanation: Thin projection lines guide accurate transfer of features and keep the final drawing readable.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply projection-line technique to align orthographic views.

questions.prompt: A learner is drawing a simple L-shaped block orthographically. Which views are usually enough to describe its shape clearly?
options: Front view, plan view, and one end view
Only the title block
Only a coloured picture
Only a material list
questions.correctAnswer: Front view, plan view, and one end view
questions.explanation: Three principal views often provide enough information to show length, height, depth, and steps in a block.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable orthographic views for simple shaped objects.

questions.prompt: A cube has edges of 40 mm. In an isometric drawing at full size, how long should each isometric edge be drawn?
options: 40 mm
20 mm
80 mm
4 mm
questions.correctAnswer: 40 mm
questions.explanation: In a basic full-size isometric drawing, object lengths are transferred along isometric axes at their actual measurement.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply isometric measurements to draw simple solids.

questions.prompt: In cabinet oblique, a box has an actual depth of 60 mm. What depth should be drawn?
options: 30 mm
60 mm
120 mm
15 mm
questions.correctAnswer: 30 mm
questions.explanation: Cabinet oblique commonly uses half depth, so 60 mm is drawn as 30 mm.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply cabinet oblique depth reduction to a simple object.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is best for drawing a rectangular box in isometric?
options: Set out isometric axes, mark length-width-height, then join corresponding edges
Shade the paper first, then guess the box size
Draw only the front rectangle and stop
Write the title block and avoid all axes
questions.correctAnswer: Set out isometric axes, mark length-width-height, then join corresponding edges
questions.explanation: Isometric drawing starts from the axes so the three dimensions remain aligned and proportional.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply steps for constructing a simple isometric object.

questions.prompt: A product has several parts that must be separated slightly in a drawing to show how they fit. Which drawing type is suitable?
options: Exploded pictorial drawing
Plain border drawing
Single hidden line
Unlabelled sketch only
questions.correctAnswer: Exploded pictorial drawing
questions.explanation: An exploded drawing shows parts separated along assembly directions so their relationships are clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Use exploded views to communicate assembly relationships.

questions.prompt: A bracket has an internal hole that is hard to understand from outside views. Which view should be added?
options: A sectional view through the hole
A random decorative border
A blank sheet
A larger price list
questions.correctAnswer: A sectional view through the hole
questions.explanation: A section through the hole reveals the internal shape and makes the feature easier to interpret.
questions.learningOutcome: Select sectional views for clarifying internal features.

questions.prompt: A sectional view cuts through two touching parts in an assembly. How can the parts be made easier to distinguish?
options: Use hatching in different directions or spacing for adjacent parts
Use the same dark solid fill on both parts
Remove all outlines and dimensions
Write the same part number on every item
questions.correctAnswer: Use hatching in different directions or spacing for adjacent parts
questions.explanation: Different hatching directions or spacing help readers separate adjacent cut materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply hatching conventions in sectional assembly drawings.

questions.prompt: Which item in an assembly drawing helps identify separate components for a parts list?
options: Part numbers or balloons
Random smudges
Erased centre lines
Unrelated slogans
questions.correctAnswer: Part numbers or balloons
questions.explanation: Part numbers or balloons link each component in the drawing to its name and quantity in a parts list.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply item numbering to identify components in assembly drawings.

questions.prompt: A cereal carton is made from a single sheet of card. Which drawing should guide cutting and folding?
options: A development with fold lines, cut lines, and glue tabs
A front view only without dimensions
A freehand circle with no labels
A safety poster about ladders only
questions.correctAnswer: A development with fold lines, cut lines, and glue tabs
questions.explanation: A package development shows the flat shape, fold positions, and joining areas needed to form the carton.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply surface development to packaging design.

questions.prompt: A cylinder has diameter 40 mm. Which measurement is needed to find the length of its rectangular development?
options: Circumference of the cylinder
Thickness of the title block
Length of the pencil
Height of the drawing table only
questions.correctAnswer: Circumference of the cylinder
questions.explanation: The curved surface of a cylinder develops into a rectangle whose length equals the cylinder circumference.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate cylinder circumference to surface development.

questions.prompt: A rectangular prism has six flat faces. What should its full development include?
options: Six connected rectangles arranged for folding
One circle and two triangles only
A single line with no fold marks
Only the front face enlarged
questions.correctAnswer: Six connected rectangles arranged for folding
questions.explanation: Each face of the prism must appear in the net so it can fold into the complete solid.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply nets to develop simple prism surfaces.

questions.prompt: A learner wants all visible outlines in CAD to print thicker than construction lines. Which CAD practice is most suitable?
options: Assign different line weights or layers before plotting
Save every line with the same colour and weight
Delete all outlines before printing
Draw the title block in a photo app only
questions.correctAnswer: Assign different line weights or layers before plotting
questions.explanation: CAD layers and line weights control how different drawing elements appear on screen and in print.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply CAD layer and plotting settings to produce readable drawings.

questions.prompt: A CAD drawing must be shared for editing next week. Which action best protects progress?
options: Save the file with a clear name and keep a backup copy
Leave it unsaved on the classroom computer
Rename every file as final without dates
Delete earlier versions before checking the new one
questions.correctAnswer: Save the file with a clear name and keep a backup copy
questions.explanation: Clear naming and backup copies reduce the risk of losing digital design work.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe file management practices for CAD projects.

questions.prompt: A school wants a wall-mounted suggestion box. Which first step best begins the design process?
options: Write a brief stating users, purpose, size limits, material, and security needs
Cut plywood before measuring the wall
Paint a box without deciding its use
Copy a random product with no user research
questions.correctAnswer: Write a brief stating users, purpose, size limits, material, and security needs
questions.explanation: A clear brief defines the problem and constraints before ideas and drawings are developed.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply design-brief writing to a school-based design problem.

questions.prompt: A learner is designing a phone stand from cardboard. Which test best checks stability?
options: Place a phone model on it and observe whether it tips or bends
Only count the number of sketches
Hide the prototype in a cupboard
Measure the colour of the cardboard
questions.correctAnswer: Place a phone model on it and observe whether it tips or bends
questions.explanation: Testing with a realistic load checks whether the prototype can support the intended object safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply prototype testing to evaluate product performance.

questions.prompt: A classroom stool design feels uncomfortable because the seat edge presses sharply behind the knees. Which design issue is involved?
options: Poor ergonomics
Good hidden-line use
Correct title block placement
Accurate hatch spacing only
questions.correctAnswer: Poor ergonomics
questions.explanation: Comfort and safe body support are ergonomic concerns in product design.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ergonomic reasoning to evaluate product comfort.

questions.prompt: A designer chooses recycled cardboard for a temporary display model. Which design factor is being applied?
options: Sustainability and material suitability
Ignoring all constraints
Increasing hidden detail
Avoiding prototyping
questions.correctAnswer: Sustainability and material suitability
questions.explanation: Reusing material for a temporary model can reduce waste while still meeting the model's purpose.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply sustainability considerations when selecting materials for design tasks.

questions.prompt: A drawing of a school notice-board bracket has neat outlines but no scale, material, or title block. What is the biggest communication weakness?
options: The maker may not know the drawing identity, size relationship, or material context
The visible outlines are too useful
The drawing has too many safety goggles
The bracket will automatically assemble itself
questions.correctAnswer: The maker may not know the drawing identity, size relationship, or material context
questions.explanation: A complete technical drawing needs identifying details and scale information as well as the object shape.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse completeness of technical drawing information.

questions.prompt: A learner dimensions a plate by chaining many small lengths across the full width. Why might datum dimensioning be better?
options: It reduces accumulated error from one feature to the next
It removes every measurement from the drawing
It makes the plate invisible
It changes all holes into squares
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces accumulated error from one feature to the next
questions.explanation: Datum dimensioning measures features from one reference, so errors do not build up across chained dimensions.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the effect of different dimensioning methods on manufacturing accuracy.

questions.prompt: A drawing shows a hole with a visible outline in the front view even though the hole is behind the front surface. What correction is needed?
options: Use hidden lines for the unseen hole edges
Make the hole outline thicker than the border
Erase the centre line and title block
Shade the entire drawing black
questions.correctAnswer: Use hidden lines for the unseen hole edges
questions.explanation: Unseen edges must be shown with hidden-line convention, not with visible outline lines.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse line-use errors in orthographic drawings.

questions.prompt: Two orthographic views of a block disagree: the plan shows a 30 mm depth but the end view shows 40 mm depth. What should be done first?
options: Check projection alignment and dimensions before redrawing the inconsistent view
Choose the larger number without checking
Remove both views and keep only a sketch
Ignore the difference because views need not match
questions.correctAnswer: Check projection alignment and dimensions before redrawing the inconsistent view
questions.explanation: Orthographic views must agree; projection and dimension checks help identify the source of inconsistency.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse consistency between related orthographic views.

questions.prompt: A front view, plan, and end view are all correct, but they are placed randomly on the sheet. What problem can this cause?
options: Readers may misinterpret which views correspond to each other
The object becomes physically larger
The pencil becomes blunt immediately
The scale changes from 1:1 to 1:10 by itself
questions.correctAnswer: Readers may misinterpret which views correspond to each other
questions.explanation: Standard view arrangement helps readers connect matching features across orthographic views.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the importance of standard orthographic view placement.

questions.prompt: An isometric drawing of a box uses one receding axis at 15 degrees and another at 45 degrees. Why is this a problem?
options: The axes are inconsistent, so the 3D form is distorted
All isometric axes must be vertical
The drawing has too many dimensions
The title block becomes unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: The axes are inconsistent, so the 3D form is distorted
questions.explanation: Isometric axes need consistent directions so the pictorial drawing represents the object clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse common errors in isometric drawings.

questions.prompt: A cavalier oblique drawing of a long cabinet looks badly stretched. Which change would most improve its appearance?
options: Use cabinet oblique with half-depth receding lines
Make the front face smaller without scale
Remove all depth lines
Add more hidden lines to the title block
questions.correctAnswer: Use cabinet oblique with half-depth receding lines
questions.explanation: Half-depth receding lines reduce visual distortion in long objects drawn obliquely.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse pictorial projection choices for clear presentation.

questions.prompt: A sectional drawing of a solid shaft shows hidden lines behind the cutting plane, making the view crowded. What is the best judgement?
options: Unnecessary hidden detail should usually be omitted when the section already explains the feature
All hidden lines must always be shown in every section
The hatching should be replaced by a border
The section should have no visible outlines
questions.correctAnswer: Unnecessary hidden detail should usually be omitted when the section already explains the feature
questions.explanation: Sectional views are meant to clarify internal form, so unnecessary hidden lines can reduce readability.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse readability of sectional drawings.

questions.prompt: An assembly drawing has five parts but no part numbers or parts list. What is the likely production problem?
options: Workers may not identify each component and quantity correctly
The drawing will automatically show material strength
The exploded view will become a section view
All components will become identical
questions.correctAnswer: Workers may not identify each component and quantity correctly
questions.explanation: Part identification links drawing components to names, materials, and quantities needed for assembly.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse missing information in assembly drawings.

questions.prompt: A development for a rectangular carton has all panels but no fold lines. What is the main risk?
options: The maker may cut correctly but fold the carton in wrong positions
The carton will need no glue tab
The paper will draw its own lines
The carton will become cylindrical
questions.correctAnswer: The maker may cut correctly but fold the carton in wrong positions
questions.explanation: Fold lines guide where panels bend, so they are essential in package developments.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the effect of missing fold information in developments.

questions.prompt: A cylindrical label development is too short around the bottle and leaves a gap. What was most likely underestimated?
options: The circumference of the bottle
The height of the title block
The number of CAD layers
The darkness of construction lines
questions.correctAnswer: The circumference of the bottle
questions.explanation: The label length must match the distance around the cylinder, which is its circumference.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse errors in cylindrical surface development.

questions.prompt: A CAD file has visible outlines, dimensions, centre lines, and construction lines all on one layer. Why can this slow editing?
options: Different elements cannot be hidden, locked, or plotted separately
The computer cannot display any line
The drawing will become a paper sketch only
The dimensions will calculate material cost automatically
questions.correctAnswer: Different elements cannot be hidden, locked, or plotted separately
questions.explanation: Separating elements into layers makes CAD drawings easier to edit, review, and print.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the effect of layer organisation on CAD workflow.

questions.prompt: A printed CAD drawing is too small to read even though the digital model is correct. Which setting should be checked first?
options: Plot scale and paper size
Keyboard colour
Mouse pad texture
File icon shape
questions.correctAnswer: Plot scale and paper size
questions.explanation: Plot settings control how the digital drawing is fitted and scaled on printed paper.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse CAD printing problems related to scale and sheet setup.

questions.prompt: A learner copies a product design from the internet and submits it without acknowledgement. Which design value is mainly violated?
options: Integrity in use of other people's ideas
Accuracy in drawing circles
Correct use of centre lines
Proper storage of compasses
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity in use of other people's ideas
questions.explanation: Design work should respect intellectual property by acknowledging sources and developing original thinking.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ethical issues in design research and presentation.

questions.prompt: A design for a classroom book rack uses attractive shapes but falls over when loaded. Which evaluation criterion has failed most?
options: Stability and function
Colour harmony only
Lettering style only
Border neatness only
questions.correctAnswer: Stability and function
questions.explanation: A product must perform safely and reliably, not only look attractive.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse product designs using functional criteria.

questions.prompt: A group wants to design a handwashing station for younger learners. Which user factor should be analysed first?
options: Height and reach of the intended users
The number of hidden lines in a bracket
The colour of the CAD icon
The price of unrelated electronics
questions.correctAnswer: Height and reach of the intended users
questions.explanation: The design must fit the users physically so they can operate it safely and comfortably.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse user characteristics when developing practical products.

questions.prompt: A prototype works well but uses a material that absorbs water for an outdoor product. What should the designer reconsider?
options: Material suitability for the operating environment
Whether sketches should be erased
Whether the title block needs a date
Whether hidden lines should be dashed
questions.correctAnswer: Material suitability for the operating environment
questions.explanation: Outdoor products need materials that can withstand expected weather and use conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse material choices against product use conditions.

questions.prompt: A design brief says a desk organiser must be low-cost, safe, and made from available school materials. Which idea best fits the constraints?
options: A cardboard organiser with folded compartments and rounded exposed edges
A heavy steel cabinet needing unavailable machines
A glass box with sharp open edges
A product with no compartments or user testing
questions.correctAnswer: A cardboard organiser with folded compartments and rounded exposed edges
questions.explanation: The cardboard organiser best matches cost, safety, availability, and functional requirements.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse design ideas against brief requirements and constraints.

questions.prompt: A learner receives feedback that a handle is too narrow for comfortable grip. Which redesign response is strongest?
options: Increase grip width, round the edges, and retest with users
Ignore the feedback because the sketch is neat
Remove the handle and keep the same brief
Only change the product colour
questions.correctAnswer: Increase grip width, round the edges, and retest with users
questions.explanation: Good redesign responds to evidence, improves comfort and safety, and checks whether the change works.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse feedback and select appropriate product improvements.

questions.prompt: A drawing has accurate dimensions but the lettering is uneven and hard to read. What is the most likely effect?
options: Important notes may be misunderstood during making
The object dimensions automatically become wrong
The drawing becomes an isometric view
The product material becomes stronger
questions.correctAnswer: Important notes may be misunderstood during making
questions.explanation: Clear lettering is part of technical communication because notes, labels, and dimensions must be read correctly.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the importance of clear lettering and annotation in technical drawings.

questions.prompt: A class must design a low-cost, foldable tablet stand for shared use in a school library. Which design plan is most complete?
options: Research user needs, write constraints, sketch alternatives, model the best idea, test stability, then prepare working drawings
Cut the first material found and paint it before testing
Use only one sketch and avoid dimensions
Ask users after producing many final stands
questions.correctAnswer: Research user needs, write constraints, sketch alternatives, model the best idea, test stability, then prepare working drawings
questions.explanation: A complete process moves from understanding the need to testing and communicating a refined solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a structured plan for solving a practical design problem.

questions.prompt: You must prepare a drawing package for a simple wooden desk organiser. Which set is most useful for production?
options: Orthographic working drawing, key dimensions, material notes, and an isometric presentation view
Only a coloured front sketch without measurements
Only a list of classmates who like the product
Only a photo of unrelated furniture
questions.correctAnswer: Orthographic working drawing, key dimensions, material notes, and an isometric presentation view
questions.explanation: Production needs accurate working information, while the pictorial view helps users visualise the final product.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a suitable drawing package for making a simple product.

questions.prompt: A learner must improve an unstable cardboard prototype without increasing cost much. Which redesign choice is best?
options: Widen the base, add folded triangular supports, and retest with the intended load
Add expensive metal parts without checking the brief
Paint it brighter and ignore the tipping problem
Remove the base to use less cardboard
questions.correctAnswer: Widen the base, add folded triangular supports, and retest with the intended load
questions.explanation: A wider base and folded supports can improve stability using the same low-cost material, and retesting checks the change.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical improvements based on prototype testing.

questions.prompt: A school project requires a package for fragile handmade badges sold at an exhibition. Which development plan best fits the task?
options: A card net with fold lines, glue tab, badge compartments, label space, and material-efficient layout
A single rectangle with no fold lines or protection
A cylindrical label only, with no package body
A random isometric box without a cutting pattern
questions.correctAnswer: A card net with fold lines, glue tab, badge compartments, label space, and material-efficient layout
questions.explanation: The package development should protect the badges, communicate product details, and use sheet material efficiently.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a package development that meets function, communication, and material-use needs.

questions.prompt: A learner is setting up a CAD template for class projects. Which setup is most professional?
options: Standard paper size, border, title block, layers for outlines and dimensions, units, and text style
A blank file with no units and all lines on one layer
A photo background with no drawing scale
A file named drawing with no backup plan
questions.correctAnswer: Standard paper size, border, title block, layers for outlines and dimensions, units, and text style
questions.explanation: A template saves time and improves consistency by setting key drawing standards before work begins.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a CAD setup that supports accurate and consistent technical drawings.

questions.prompt: A group must present a redesigned school bag hook to a review panel. Which presentation evidence is strongest?
options: Brief, user research summary, sketches, selected working drawing, prototype test results, and improvement notes
Only the final colour choice
Only a verbal claim that the hook is strong
Only the names of group members
questions.correctAnswer: Brief, user research summary, sketches, selected working drawing, prototype test results, and improvement notes
questions.explanation: Strong design presentation uses evidence from the whole process, not only the final appearance.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an evidence-based presentation for a design solution.

questions.prompt: A learner needs to plan drawings for a small assembly with a base, two side plates, and a pin. Which drawing sequence is best?
options: Sketch the assembled idea, draw each part with dimensions, then prepare an assembly or exploded view
Start with a parts list only and never draw the parts
Draw only the pin and ignore the base
Make a section view before deciding how parts fit
questions.correctAnswer: Sketch the assembled idea, draw each part with dimensions, then prepare an assembly or exploded view
questions.explanation: Part drawings define individual components, while an assembly or exploded view explains how they fit together.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a drawing sequence for communicating a simple assembly.

questions.prompt: A community notice stand must be durable, readable, low-cost, and safe near a school gate. Which design response best balances these needs?
options: Use a stable frame, weather-resistant board, rounded edges, clear lettering, and maintainable local materials
Use thin wet cardboard with sharp corners and tiny text
Use costly imported material without checking availability
Make a beautiful sketch but omit dimensions and safety checks
questions.correctAnswer: Use a stable frame, weather-resistant board, rounded edges, clear lettering, and maintainable local materials
questions.explanation: The best response balances function, safety, readability, cost, maintenance, and the real use environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a balanced design response for a local practical need.
